subject: POC trial: Model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel@nearshore.ai>, Elena Gomez <elena@fabrica.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + POC plan (model selection)

Hi Daniel and Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the POC: 

1) Goals / success criteria (draft):
- 90th percentile inference latency under 600ms for 1k daily active users (text completion flows).
- >= 86% top-1 accuracy on your internal FAQ matching evaluation (we'll formalize eval set).
- Multilingual: Spanish and Portuguese quality parity within a 5% delta vs. English in those tests.
- No customer PII leaves your VPC (we'll use Private deployment or dedicated routing).

2) Evaluation plan / deliverables:
- Shared prompt set & 1500-eval-case spreadsheet from Fabrica by 2026-03-05.
- Redwood runs baseline on three open models, returns metrics (latency, tokens/cost, quality): recommended shortlist: Llama-2-13B-chat, Mistral-7B-chat, and a multilingual candidate (XGLM or BLOOMZ variant).
- We include a fallback smaller model for cost-sensitive paths.
- Deliverable: POC report with: quantitative metrics, example failures, prompt tuning suggestions, and recommended model & deployment config.

3) Timeline:
- Mar 5: Fabrica provides eval set + representative traffic profile (QPS, average prompt length).
- Mar 9: Redwood provision POC infra and upload models; initial runs begin.
- Mar 13: Preliminary results and sync call.
- Mar 20: Final POC report & recommended rollout plan.

4) Ownership:
- Fabrica: supply eval cases, designate a technical contact for data access (Elena).
- Redwood: Ben (sales lead) + Marissa (inference/ops) + Jordan (solutions) execute the POC.

5) Action items (for today):
- Elena: share the 1500-case eval spreadsheet and a short sample of multilingual prompts (by Mar 5).
- Daniel: confirm whether you want us to test the PII redaction flow or assume data is already de-identified.
- Marissa/Jordan: recommend initial model shortlist and configuration (Ben will follow up below).

Attachments: attaching a simple POC template (fabrica-poc-plan.xlsx) and sample prompts.

Thanks — we'll keep the first iteration narrow and measurable.

Best,
Ben

Ben — very helpful summary, thanks. Elena and I talked this afternoon and agree with the plan. A few clarifications / additions to success criteria: 

- For the customer-facing completions (checkout assistant), we need hallucination rate under 4% on fact-based queries (we'll provide labeled examples).
- For latency SLO, if we can get 95th percentile below 1s that will be fine for the web flows; mobile needs ideally <700ms.
- Multilingual: Spanish is the highest priority, Portuguese a close second. We have ~12% of traffic in Spanish today.

We will:
- Share the eval sheet and a 200-record Spanish + 100-record Portuguese sample (by 2026-03-05).
- Confirm that data will be uploaded to the POC bucket and redacted according to our template (we'll indicate PII rows).

One risk to call out: we have customers in EU and need to understand where inference runs for EU traffic (we may want region-based routing). If you can flag that in the POC report that'd be great.

Thanks,
Daniel

Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap + POC plan (model selection) — recommendation

Thanks Ben — quick recommendation from the inference team based on the constraints: 

Primary model (recommended): Llama-2-13B-chat (int8 quantized where possible)
- Why: strong general-purpose instruction-following performance, good latency/cost profile on our infra for completion-style tasks, widely reproducible.
- Multilingual: good baseline performance in Spanish; for higher Spanish fidelity we will apply language-specific prompt templates and a small in-POC prompt tuning pass (few-shot examples).

Fallback (cost-sensitive): Mistral-7B-chat (int8)
- Why: excellent cost-performance; slightly lower quality on some nuanced factual queries but performs well for template-driven assistant responses. Good for bursty/low-cost paths.

Multilingual specialist (if needed): BLOOMZ-7B1-mt or XGLM-7B (evaluate early)
- Why: explicit multilingual training can improve Spanish/Portuguese parity. We recommend running 200 Spanish + 100 Portuguese cases against this candidate to validate uplift.

Other config notes:
- Quantization: try int8 quantized inference for both primary and fallback during the POC; we can also run one 4-bit quantized pass if latency remains acceptable to estimate further savings.
- KV cache and prefix caching: enable for the most common prompts (checkout flows) to lower latency on repeated sessions. We will instrument per-route caching in the POC infra.
- Safety/hallucination checks: add a factuality regression test against the labeled set (Daniel will provide labels). We'll report hallucination rate and top failure modes.

Resource and ETA: 
- Provisioning: we can have the POC infra provisioned on dedicated nodes by Mar 8 (one day earlier than target) if we get the eval set by Mar 5.
- Recommended infra: 1x A100-80GB equivalent for baseline runs + 2xA10/GPU instances for parallel cheaper fallback runs. If we run 4-bit perf tests we may need an extra slot for compilation runs.

Next steps / action items: 
- Ben: confirm we should include BLOOMZ/XGLM candidate (cost + time to evaluate ~2 extra days).
- Elena / Daniel: upload eval set by Mar 5 and indicate PII rows.
- Jordan: please draft the prompt templates (Spanish/Portuguese augmentations) and share by Mar 6.

I attached a short sample prompt file (sample-prompts.txt) with a few Spanish prompt variations we plan to test.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Inference | Redwood Inference
